name: Loganberry
grown_as: A hybrid berry between blackberry and raspberry, trained on wires. The library also gives this drawing to William's tayberry ('Buckingham', thornless) and tummelberry, which look much the same; tayberry fruit is longer and brighter red.
habit: Long, trailing to arching canes, 2 to 3 m, trained on wires. Canes green to reddish, with scattered small prickles (some forms thornless). Canes fruit in their second year then die.

leaf.type: Compound: three or five leaflets, pinnate like raspberry
leaf.leaflets: The end leaflet the largest, on its own stalk; side leaflets almost stalkless
leaf.outline: Each leaflet broadly oval, 5 to 10 cm long
leaf.margin: Coarse, sharp, double teeth all round
leaf.veins: Straight side veins pressed in, so the leaflet looks pleated
leaf.surface: Rich green above; paler and softly downy beneath, but not white

flower.form: An open flower, larger and flatter than raspberry
flower.centre: Many white stamens round a green dome of pistils
flower.carried: In small clusters at the ends of the side shoots

fruit: Long, cone-shaped to cylindrical, 2.5 to 4 cm, of many hairy drupelets; dark red to deep red-purple when fully ripe. Keeps its core when picked. In small hanging clusters, unripe green and red ones beside ripe. July to August.
seedling: Not drawn: grown as bought plants
winter: Bare canes, green to reddish, tied along wires.

leaf: three or five leaflets, end leaflet on its own stalk
broad oval leaflets with coarse double teeth
bloom: a ring of white stamens round a green centre
young: leaves of three or five leaflets
flower: small clusters of white flowers at the ends of side shoots
crop: long cone-shaped dark red fruit hanging in small clusters
green and red unripe fruit beside the ripe

look_alikes: Raspberry fruit is round and pulls off its core; its leaves are white beneath. Blackberry fruit ripens black and its leaflets spread from one point. Japanese wineberry is covered in red bristles.
